title: incremental-weight-streaming-and-mmap-strategy
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a practical runtime strategy for incremental weight streaming + mmap-backed residency for server-side models. Goal: enable low-memory startup (fast cold availability), deterministic memory residency for hot models, and safe, low-latency hot-swap/rollout semantics that interact cleanly with the scheduler and KV cache. This is a working design — focuses on engineering trade-offs and operational knobs rather than research-first descriptions.

Motivation / problems we must solve:
- Large model binaries (10s–100s GB) make full eager load impractical for rapid scale-up or for nodes with mixed occupancy.
- Existing mmap-only approach can yield unpredictable page-fault patterns and high first-request latency if the OS page-cache is cold.
- Safetensors and other modern formats reduce parse cost but need a clear path for streaming into GPU/CPU memory and fallbacks for unsupported formats.
- Hot-swap/rollout must preserve KV-cache correctness and avoid silently dropping in-flight requests or corrupting cached KV state.
- Scheduler must be able to make placement decisions with partial-weight knowledge (e.g., model supports incremental readiness levels).

High-level approach summary:
- Two-layer residency model: on-disk file(s) -> mmap-readable backing -> in-memory residency (pinned CPU pages or CUDA buffers).
- Incremental streaming loader: progressive phases (metadata-only, essential-weights, attention-kernel-weights, remaining-weights). Each phase sets a readiness level exposed to scheduler/health checks.
- Files always published in safetensors (preferred) or converted on ingest to a streaming-friendly bundle. On-disk layout organized by shard + chunk to permit sub-file reads.
- Use mmap for stable addressability and minimal copy for large static tensors; use proactive prefetch/pinning for critical tensors to reduce first-token latency.
- Hot-swap performed as atomic pointer-swap with KV-cache reconciliation and drain semantics for in-flight sequences.

On-disk layout / artifact format:
- Canonical artifact: <model>.rwd.bundle (zstd-framed tar style but with index) that contains:
  - manifest.json (version, shard map, tensor index, hash per chunk)
  - metadata.safetensors (model config + tensor shapes/types)
  - shards/ (shard-0000.safetensors, shard-0001.safetensors...)
  - optional: mmap_hints.bin (page-alignment hints generated at conversion time)
- Each shard broken into fixed-size chunks (default 16MB) with chunk-level checksums. The manifest maps tensor->(shard, offset, length, chunk-list).
- Conversion pipeline on ingest will produce this bundle from upstream checkpoints (torch, huggingface, safetensors) and also generate the mmap_hints.

Loader lifecycle and readiness levels:
- READY_LEVELS: metadata_only -> core_loaded -> attention_ready -> warm -> full_ready
  - metadata_only: manifest and shapes parsed. Router can show model as "registered" but placement is blocked or flagged low-capacity.
  - core_loaded: embedding matrix + final logits head loaded and pinned -> can serve short completion/lightweight evals.
  - attention_ready: all attention and feedforward weights for first N layers pinned; first-token latency should be close to steady-state for typical prompts.
  - warm: >80% of chunks present in page cache or pinned; targeted SLOs met for expected workload.
  - full_ready: all tensor chunks resident (same as old eager load).
- Each level has a well-defined health probe and metric tags (model:version, level). Scheduler uses level to decide where to route and whether to allow new long-running sessions.

Streaming strategy and heuristics:
- Prioritization order (default): embedding + head -> early attention layers -> later layers -> MLPs -> positional/other small tensors
- Heuristics based on workload and historical traces: if average sequence length < 64 and concurrency high, prefer core_loaded + attention_ready; if RLHF-like workloads with long contexts, target higher early.
- Adaptive parallel fetchers: loader issues parallel ranged reads for chunk lists, with a global cap per node to avoid saturating disk or network. Cap is dynamic: base cap derived from node storage bandwidth and current cpu/io pressure.
- Prefetch window: during active inference, maintain a sliding window of next-k chunks for the current session's KV growth estimate (derived from past token growth patterns).

mmap usage and pinning policy:
- Open shard files with MAP_SHARED and maintain file descriptors in the loader process.
- For each chunk we want fast access to, call madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) then attempt to mlock a small pinned subset of pages (bounded by config) to ensure kernel doesn't evict during heavy inference.
- For GPU memory moves, prefer cudaMemcpyAsync from pinned host pages to device buffers. This avoids staged page-fault copies.
- We avoid mlock-ing entire shards by default — only 1–2GB pinned per GPU as operator-configured ceiling.

Safetensors and conversion details:
- Prefer safetensors because of predictable binary offsets and no Python pickle semantics.
- On ingest, we run a conversion to the bundle format and generate index. Conversion also identifies small/large tensors: small tensors (<1MB) are consolidated into a "small.tensors" file for efficient load and parsing.
- For any non-safetensors input, an automated conversion service will run with reproducible hashing and immutability guarantee; conversion artifacts stored in model-artifact-store with lifecycle policies.

Hot-swap / atomic rollout procedure:
- Goals: no request sees mixed model versions in a single sequence; minimal disruption for long-lived sessions; fast rollback.
- Operator publishes new bundle version -> control plane signals selected nodes to prepare for swap.
- Node follows steps: 1) stage new bundle metadata (metadata_only), 2) start streaming essential chunks in background to reach core_loaded, 3) drain new request routing to keep in-flight sequences on old model (graceful drain window), 4) when no active sessions remain or after max_wait, perform atomic swap: install new pointer table and update readiness tag, 5) reconcile KV-cache (see below) and start serving new requests.
- Rollback: keep old bundle available in a short-term LRU cache for immediate fallback. Rollback triggers pointer-swap back, and reverse reconciliation.

KV-cache coherence and migration:
- We treat KV entries as versioned objects: key structure includes (model_id, model_version, layer, token_index_range).
- During hot-swap, we must avoid reusing old KV entries incompatible with new model layout/weights. Migration strategies:
  - Incompatible model.version: invalidate KV-cache for affected sessions (explicit invalidation API).
  - Compatible topology but different weights: keep KV contents but attach weight-version tag; when serving, loader consults a compatibility function to decide to accept or regenerate KV entries.
- For long-lived sessions where we must preserve context, we prefer to warm new model by replaying key slices (background fetch + re-computation of KV for recent tokens) before switching routing. This is expensive but ensures continuity for a small percentage of sessions (configurable).

Scheduler integration and placement decisions:
- Model readiness levels emitted as node-local capability flags to the scheduler (k/v: model:model_id:version -> readiness_level).
- Placement policy uses readiness_level as a first-order filter: do not place high-SLO requests on nodes < attention_ready unless fallback policy configured.
- Scheduler maintains per-node bandwidth and current staged-download budget. When scaling replicas, scheduler will prefer nodes with free staged-download budget to amortize fetch cost.
- Pre-warm hints: API to request pre-warm for a set of nodes (used by Dedicated and Private deployments for capacity commitments).

Observability and metrics:
- Metrics to export (labels include model_id, model_version, node_id):
  - model_load.time_to_level.{metadata_only,core_loaded,attention_ready,full_ready}
  - model_load.bytes_streamed
  - model_load.chunk_fetch_latency_pXX/median
  - page_faults_during_inference_per_minute
  - pinned_pages_bytes
  - hot_swap.duration and hot_swap.rollback_count
  - kv_cache.invalidations and kv_migrations
- Tracing: span for bundle -> shard -> chunk to identify load hotspots. Correlate first-token latency to chunk availability.

Operational knobs and configs (examples):
- chunk_size (default 16MB)
- max_parallel_fetches_per_node (default 8)
- pinned_pages_limit_per_node (default 1.5GB)
- readiness_timeouts (per-level)
- hot_swap_drain_window_seconds (default 30–300s depending on tier)
- kv_migration_policy: [invalidate, best-effort-migrate, replay-recompute]

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Disk bandwidth saturation: backpressure loader and update scheduler to avoid dispatching more pre-warms; fall back to cold-hosting that uses eager load on nodes with spare bandwidth.
- Corrupted chunk: manifest-level checksum mismatch -> fail load and fallback to previous bundle. Alert and mark artifact bad in artifact store.
- Page-fault storms for cold mmap: proactively madvise + read-ahead first N chunks at core_loaded to avoid worst-case tail latency.
- Hot-swap hung due to long-lived sessions: configurable max_wait after which we force-swap with session abort metrics exposed. Use tiering to allow longer waits for enterprise customers.

Testing, rollout and canary plan:
- Unit tests for chunk indexing, checksum verification, and manifest parse.
- Integration tests: simulate networks with slow storage, verify readiness transitions are observed by scheduler, and SLO behavior for short and long contexts.
- Canary rollout: roll new loader binary + feature flag to 1–2 nodes per region, measure model_load.time_to_level.* and first_token_latency, increase if stable.

Operator UX / CLI snippets (examples):
- rwdctl model prewarm --model-id gpt-large-v2 --nodes node-12,node-17 --target-level attention_ready
- rwdctl model swap --model-id gpt-large-v2 --from v12 --to v13 --drain 120s --kv-policy replay-recompute
- rwdctl model status --model-id gpt-large-v2 --node node-17 -> shows readiness_level and bytes_streamed

Open questions / future work:
- Better kernel-level integration: explore io_uring-based prefetch and async page population to reduce overhead and userland copying.
- Hybrid compressed-on-disk + decode-on-demand for quantized weights to reduce network IO for cold start.
- Fine-grained GPU residency controller that can migrate layer buffers across GPUs when capacity shifts.

Appendix: quick sequence diagrams (text form)
- Normal load:
  control-plane -> node: publish bundle vX
  node: parse manifest (metadata_only) -> scheduler update
  node: start parallel chunk fetches -> core_loaded -> advertise
  node: continue background stream to attention_ready -> warm -> full_ready

- Hot-swap:
  operator -> control-plane: request deploy vY
  control-plane -> nodes: stage vY (metadata_only)
  nodes: stream core tensors for vY in background
  router: stop routing new sessions to nodes during drain window
  after drain: node atomic swap pointers, reconcile KV-cache, mark new readiness

Notes and references:
- See GH PR 894 for initial mmap prototype and early madvise experiments.
- Related Jira INF-4829: KV-cache migration proposal.

End of draft. Comments welcome — especially on heuristics for prefetch size and hot-swap drain semantics.
